Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=andesim path=driver/elf_syms.cpp lines=120-125 kind=dead-code-block
Claim: elf_entry() is an unused function left over from the removed cosim/lock-step feature; its header comment still describes it as 'the default lock-step arm pc'.
Evidence given: grep -rn elf_entry across driver/, tests/, scripts/ and the vsim repo finds only elf_syms.hpp:26-28 (decl+comment) and elf_syms.cpp:120-125 (def) -- zero call sites, no test. Added in 992b9bf 'run --model cycle --cosim -- lock-step DV co-simulation' ('elf_syms: elf_entry (default arm pc)'); the cosim/lockstep family was removed in ff20602/e6199cf. symbolize/fn_range from the same file ARE used (hotloops.cpp:175,182,642).

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?
If ANY live reference or intentional-keep reason exists, verdict isLegacy=false. Default to false when uncertain. If true, give the exact deleteScope.

1	// ELF symbol resolution for pc-trigger boundaries (F9).
2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.
10	#ifndef ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
11	#define ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
12	
13	#include <cstdint>
14	#include <string>
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Resolve a pc-mode boundary to a bare hex address string (no "0x" prefix).
19	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
20	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
21	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
22	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
23	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,
24	                       std::string& err);
25	
26	// The ELF entry point (e_entry) -- the default lock-step arm pc. Returns 0 and
27	// sets `err` on an unreadable / non-RV64 file; clears `err` on success.
28	uint64_t elf_entry(const std::string& elf_path, std::string& err);
29	
30	// The ELF class width in bits from e_ident[EI_CLASS]: 32 (ELFCLASS32) or 64
31	// (ELFCLASS64). Returns 0 when `elf_path` is unreadable or not an ELF. Reads
32	// only the 16-byte e_ident (the class-independent prefix), so it answers for
33	// rv32 and rv64 alike -- the source of truth for the fast auto-pick of
34	// qemu-system-riscv32/64 and the cycle/hybrid arch-match guard.
35	int elf_xlen(const std::string& elf_path);
36	
37	// L26/F3: the highest byte of the ELF's static memory image -- the maximum
38	// (p_paddr + p_memsz) over PT_LOAD segments. The driver rejects a hybrid run
39	// when this exceeds the V-scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size): the static image
40	// would extend into the reserved transport page above the program's RAM.
41	// Returns 0 + err on an unreadable / non-ELFCLASS64 file; 0 with empty err when
42	// the ELF has no loadable segments (nothing to clash with the scratch).
43	uint64_t elf_load_top(const std::string& elf_path, std::string& err);
44	
45	// Reverse lookup: the nearest function symbol at or below `addr`, formatted
46	// "name+0xoff" (or just "name" at offset 0). Returns "" when no covering
47	// function symbol is found or the ELF is unreadable -- the caller always has
48	// the raw pc to fall back on, so this never errors.
49	std::string symbolize(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
50	
51	// Returns {st_value, st_value + st_size} for the FUNC symbol covering `addr`.
52	// Both members are 0 when not found or unreadable.
53	std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> fn_range(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
54	
55	}  // namespace andes_sim
56	
57	#endif  // ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
58

input.deleteScope: driver/elf_syms.cpp lines 120-125 (elf_entry definition) and driver/elf_syms.hpp lines 26-28 (its comment + declaration). The rest of elf_syms.{hpp,cpp} stays: resolve_pc/elf_xlen/elf_load_top are used by the driver and symbolize/fn_range by hotloops.cpp.
input.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on every axis. (1) Read the code: elf_entry is defined at driver/elf_syms.cpp:120-125 and declared at driver/elf_syms.hpp:28 with a comment (lines 26-27) still calling it "the default lock-step arm pc" - a reference to the removed cosim feature. (2) git grep of all tracked files in andesim finds exactly those two occurrences (decl + def), zero call sites anywhere (driver/, tests/, scripts/, docs, Makefiles, CMake); git grep in /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim finds zero hits. Being a namespaced C++ function, it can only be invoked by literal name, so no glob/variable-built indirect usage is possible. (3) History confirms the story: before ff20602 its only caller was driver/cmd_run.cpp:295 (`arm_pc = elf_entry(elf_path, err);` - the cosim lock-step arm pc). Commit ff20602 "Remove icount trigger, simpoint-driven trigger, and cosim features" deleted the caller and even scrubbed the cosim wording from the neighboring symbolize() comment, but left elf_entry and its stale lock-step comment behind. Later commits touching the file (elf_load_top, elf_xlen, symbolize/fn_range for hotloops) added other functions, not callers of elf_entry. (4) CLAUDE.md lists cosim as removed and pc mode requires explicit --pc-start/--pc-end (no e_entry default), so there is no intentional-fallback rationale like semihost_exit.inc. (5) symbolize/fn_range in the same file ARE live (driver/hotloops.cpp:175,182,642), so only the function, not the file, is dead. Removing an uncalled free function plus its declaration cannot break the build.
